positive_cases.why_used: To aggregate multiple European soft-money funds and access Eurimages, requiring multilateral status as no single minority partner hit 20%.
positive_cases.legal_mechanism: European Convention on Cinematographic Co-Production (lowering minimum to 10%).
positive_cases.economic_rationale: Maximized non-recoupable soft money; leveraged regional German funds for post-production.
positive_cases.practice_source: Eurimages project lists, Screen International case studies.
positive_cases.generalizable_lesson: If bilateral 20% minimum is unreachable, adding a 3rd European partner unlocks the 10% multilateral threshold.

positive_cases.why_used: To access national treatment in both Canada and Ireland, allowing stacking of federal tax credits with national selective funds.
positive_cases.economic_rationale: The combined value of Telefilm + Screen Ireland equity + CAVCO + Section 181 far exceeded any pure service rebate.
positive_cases.generalizable_lesson: National treatment via official coproduction unlocks selective funds that drastically reduce net production cost compared to service rebates.

negative_cases.why_failed: Failed the proportionality test. The financial contribution did not match the creative/technical contribution (budget was 80% UK, but all ATL was Australian).
negative_cases.economic_rationale: Lost official status, reverted to Location Offset (lower rate) in Australia.
negative_cases.generalizable_lesson: Optimizer MUST validate that financial contribution roughly equals creative/technical points; otherwise, official status is rejected.

negative_cases.why_failed: Included $2M of deferred producer fees in the QPE base to increase the rebate.
negative_cases.legal_mechanism: CAVCO rules on incurred vs paid costs.
negative_cases.economic_rationale: CRA audited and removed the deferred fees because they were contingent on profits and not unconditionally payable, reducing the rebate by $500k.
negative_cases.practice_source: Canadian tax accounting alerts (e.g., MNP, BDO).
negative_cases.generalizable_lesson: Deferred consideration cannot be modeled as QPE unless it is an unconditional, non-contingent liability.
